text:
sara_support: FYI — customer_mike escalated: SSE stream repeatedly disconnects behind their corp proxy. They see partial JSON payloads, client reconnects, then duplicates/partials. No 5xx from our side in the snippets they sent.

customer_mike: reproducible for us. Steps: client connects via corporate gateway (h2->h1), receives 2 events, then connection drops. On reconnect we get a fragment like `\"{\"type\":\"update\",\"data\":\"{\"id\":\"123` and then a second chunk completes it — sometimes duplicated. Happens across Chrome + a custom long-lived fetch client.

sara_support: they attached a quick curl test: `curl --http2 -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?session=abc\"` — output shows JSON bodies split mid-object.

mike_oncall: Any x-request-id values? timestamps? we need to correlate with edge logs. Also is the customer going through a gRPC-web gateway or a plain HTTP proxy?

customer_mike: Their infra team says there's a middleware that translates gRPC-web -> HTTP/1.1 for legacy appliances. They suspect it does some re-chunking. They can share proxy config if needed.

alex_runtime: This smells like hop-wise re-chunking where H2 DATA frame boundaries are not preserved when translated to chunked H1. SSE expects event boundaries (double newline) but intermediaries may slice TCP/HTTP chunks arbitrarily. If server flushes partial JSON mid-event, proxies can forward partial bits separately which breaks client-side event parsing and leads to reconnects.

alex_runtime: Quick repro suggestion for eng: run an H2 client that sends long SSE events and put an H1 reverse proxy that rewrites/aggregates chunks (gRPC-web style). Observe split boundaries. Minimal curl reproduction: ```bash
# on client
curl --http2 -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://edge.local/stream?test=split\"
# on server side produce one large event and flush partials every 50 bytes
```

mike_oncall: TODOs: (1) ask customer for x-request-id on failing attempts, (2) request a copy of proxy config or a pcap if they can, (3) attempt repro in our lab with a gRPC-web transform. I'll start a lab repro.

sara_support: Customer also complained about billing — they saw retry attempts counted as separate usage for the same logical session. Could be double-charges because reconnects create new request IDs. @billing-bot can you check if repeated partial reconnects are being billed?

billing-bot: please provide the customer account_id and the two sample request ids. We'll flag for manual review and put a short-term credit hold if warranted.

customer_mike: account id: acct_4387, sample timestamps: 2025-11-03T14:12:21Z and 2025-11-03T14:12:28Z. Request ids included in headers: r-0a1b2c3d and r-0a1b2c3e.

alex_runtime: Escalation plan: I'll reproduce with a toy gRPC-web -> H1 proxy; instrument edge to capture `x-request-id` mapping when we downgrade h2->h1. Also add a short-term mitigation: make SSE events end with an explicit sentinel chunk (e.g., `\n\n`) and avoid flushing partial JSON mid-event; that reduces probability of proxy splitting meaningful tokens. We'll test if that eliminates partial parses.

mike_oncall: If we confirm proxy-induced fragmentation, we should add guidance to Support KB: "If you sit behind an intermediary that rewrites HTTP2 frames, prefer server-side event framing (event: / double-newline) or use chunk markers or switch to a websocket fallback."

alex_runtime: One more note — gRPC-web proxies often base64-encode payloads or wrap in envelopes; that can make chunk boundaries even worse. Ask customer if their middleware does envelope encoding.

sara_support: I've asked customer to (a) run a curl --http2 -v and paste full request/response headers (b) try a direct connection to our edge from an external machine (to rule out ISP/proxy) (c) share proxy config.

deploy-bot: [deploy] Lab repro environment created: edge-proxy-v2 + gRPC-web shim. Tests scheduled.

alex_runtime: After lab runs: initial repro confirmed hop-wise chunking causes event body splits on our H1-compatible path. Next steps: (1) add per-request reassembly logic in edge that buffers until a full SSE event (double newline) before forwarding to client when proxy mode is detected, (2) add telemetry to detect high partial-fragment rates and fire alerts.

mike_oncall: I'll coordinate a patch PR for the reassembly buffer and run it in a canary. Also adding a short retention log to capture raw frames for 5 failing requests for debug trace.

sara_support: Customer is ok with canary test. Keeping them updated. Thanks all — I'll post results here once we have canary data. :thumbsup:

customer_mike: thanks team, appreciate the quick help.
